The word for "gain" usually means profit made by violence or greed: the nations' plunder goes back to the true owner.

decisions.choice: the Lord of the whole earth: the LORD as master of every nation
decisions.reason: The title is used in Joshua 3:11, 13 and Psalm 97:5. The nations that gathered against Zion belong to him, and so does their wealth.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion (L); Daughter Zion (B); people of Zion (R); gain (L); plunder (B); everything they stole (R); the Lord of the whole earth (all levels)
decisions.reason: The forms for the daughter of Zion follow the wording set for the prophets. Readable says what the picture of the ox means (m1). "Lord" for the title follows the Psalms.

decisions.choice: "Chúa của cả trái đất" at every level
decisions.reason: The Adonai title, "Chúa" capitalised with no span, as the terms note gives for "'Adon" and as Zechariah 4:14 will have it.

decisions.choice: "Bwana wa dunia yote"
decisions.reason: The title as Zechariah 4:14 and the term sheet have it; "Bwana" for Adon takes no divine_name span.

decisions.choice: "온 땅의 주님" at every level
decisions.reason: The Lord (*'adon*) of the whole earth is "주님", as the term sheet [Rev 11:4]; "놋" for bronze, as the published prophets.

source.text: עַתָּה֙ תִּתְגֹּדְדִ֣י בַת־גְּד֔וּד מָצ֖וֹר שָׂ֣ם עָלֵ֑ינוּ בַּשֵּׁ֨בֶט֙ יַכּ֣וּ עַֽל־הַלְּחִ֔י אֵ֖ת שֹׁפֵ֥ט יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Now gash yourself, daughter of a troop; a siege he has set against us; with the rod they will strike on the cheek the judge of Israel.

en.L: Now gash yourself, daughter of troops; \q a siege has been laid against us; \q with the rod they strike on the cheek \q the judge of Israel.
en.B: Now gash yourself in grief, daughter of raiders; \q a siege has been laid against us. \q With a rod they strike the ruler of Israel \q on the cheek.
en.R: Now, city of soldiers, cut yourself in grief. \q Our enemies have surrounded us. \q They strike Israel's ruler on the face \q with a rod.

vi.L: Bây giờ hãy rạch mình, hỡi con gái của các đạo quân; \q người ta đã vây hãm chúng ta; \q chúng lấy roi đánh vào má \q quan xét của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Bây giờ hãy rạch mình mà than khóc, hỡi con gái của quân cướp; \q người ta đã vây hãm chúng ta. \q Chúng lấy gậy đánh người cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên \q vào má.
vi.R: Hỡi thành của các chiến binh, bây giờ hãy rạch mình mà than khóc. \q Kẻ thù đã bao vây chúng ta. \q Chúng lấy gậy đánh vào mặt \q người cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên.

fr.L: Maintenant, fais-toi des incisions, fille de troupes ; \q on a mis le siège contre nous ; \q avec le bâton ils frappent sur la joue \q le juge d’Israël.
fr.B: Maintenant, entaille-toi la peau en signe de deuil, fille de pillards ; \q on a mis le siège contre nous. \q Avec un bâton, on frappe le chef d’Israël \q sur la joue.
fr.R: Maintenant, ville de soldats, fais-toi des entailles pour montrer ta douleur. \q Nos ennemis nous ont encerclés. \q Ils frappent le chef d’Israël au visage \q avec un bâton.

es.L: Ahora hazte incisiones, hija de tropas; \q nos han puesto sitio; \q con la vara golpean en la mejilla \q al juez de Israel.
es.B: Ahora hazte cortes de dolor, hija de saqueadores; \q nos han puesto sitio. \q Con una vara golpean al gobernante de Israel \q en la mejilla.
es.R: Ahora, ciudad de soldados, hazte cortes de dolor. \q Nuestros enemigos nos han rodeado. \q Golpean en la cara al gobernante de Israel \q con una vara.

sw.L: Sasa jichanje, binti wa vikosi; \q mazingiwa yamewekwa juu yetu; \q kwa fimbo wanampiga shavuni \q mwamuzi wa Israeli.
sw.B: Sasa jichanje kwa huzuni, binti wa wavamizi; \q tumezingirwa na adui. \q Kwa fimbo wanampiga mtawala wa Israeli \q shavuni.
sw.R: Sasa, ewe mji wa askari, jikate kwa huzuni. \q Adui zetu wametuzunguka. \q Wanampiga mtawala wa Israeli usoni \q kwa fimbo.

ko.L: 이제 너는 네 몸에 상처를 내어라, 군대의 딸아. \q 그가 우리를 향하여 포위 진을 쳤다. \q 그들이 막대기로 \q 이스라엘의 재판관의 뺨을 친다.
ko.B: 약탈자들의 딸아, 이제 슬퍼하며 네 몸에 상처를 내어라. \q 적이 우리를 에워싸고 진을 쳤다. \q 그들이 막대기로 이스라엘의 통치자의 \q 뺨을 친다.
ko.R: 군인들의 성아, 이제 슬퍼하며 네 몸에 상처를 내어라. \q 원수들이 우리를 에워쌌다. \q 그들이 이스라엘의 통치자의 얼굴을 \q 막대기로 때린다.

decisions.choice: This verse is 4:14 in the Hebrew text, 5:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text ends chapter 4 with this verse. Many Bibles begin chapter 5 with it, numbering it 5:1, so their 5:2-15 is 5:1-14 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Micah is cited by the Hebrew numbers. The verse belongs with what follows as well as with what goes before: the ruler struck here is answered by the ruler promised in 5:1.

decisions.choice: gash yourself, daughter of troops: a play on two words that sound alike
alternatives: gather in troops, daughter of troops
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun are built on the same sounds. The verb can mean to cut oneself, as mourners did (Jeremiah 16:6; 47:5), or to gather in bands; the noun means a troop or raiding band. Jerusalem, a city of soldiers, is told to mourn, or to muster its troops for the siege. The ancient Greek translation read the line differently. The sense of mourning is followed here.

decisions.choice: they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek: the king is humiliated by his enemies
decisions.reason: A blow on the cheek was an insult (1 Kings 22:24; Job 16:10; Lamentations 3:30). "The judge of Israel" is the king, whose task was to judge his people; the Hebrew words for "rod" and "judge" sound alike. The leader who should rule with a rod (a scepter) is beaten with one. Christian readers have heard an echo in the soldiers who struck Jesus on the head with a reed (Matthew 27:30), but the verse itself speaks of Jerusalem's ruler under siege.

decisions.choice: daughter of troops (L); daughter of raiders (B); city of soldiers (R); in grief (B, R); judge (L); ruler (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why one gashes oneself (m2) and call the judge a ruler (m3). "Has been laid" gives the Hebrew "he has set", which names no one.

decisions.choice: "hãy rạch mình ... hỡi con gái của các đạo quân" (L)
decisions.reason: The meaning footnote: a play on two words that sound alike ("gash yourself" and "troops"); Vietnamese cannot keep the sound, so the footnote carries it. The verse is 5:1 in Bibles that follow the later numbering.

decisions.choice: "hazte incisiones, hija de tropas" (L); "hazte cortes de dolor, hija de saqueadores" (B); "ciudad de soldados" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew play on two words that sound alike cannot be kept in Spanish; each level gives the sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "jichanje, binti wa vikosi" (L); "binti wa wavamizi" (B); "ewe mji wa askari" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on two words that sound alike (footnoted meaning decision); Swahili cannot keep the sound play and translates the sense, as the English does. Hebrew 4:14 is 5:1 in many Bibles.

decisions.choice: "군대의 딸" (L); "약탈자들의 딸" (B); "군인들의 성" (R); "재판관" (L), "통치자" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The two words of the line sound alike in Hebrew (meaning decision, footnoted); Korean cannot keep the play and follows the English at each level. The verse is 5:1 in English Bibles.
